jobs.title: Research Data Analyst in Global Infectious Disease Epidemiology
jobs.description:
Department and Project Overview

The Planetary Child Health & Enterics Observatory (Plan-EO) is an interdisciplinary research initiative and living evidence system based at the University of Virginia School of Medicine and founded and coordinated by Dr. Josh Colston.

Plan-EO works to systematically model, quantify, predict, and project the epidemiology and burden of enteric infectious diseases and their risk factors across low-resource regions of the world. The initiative makes its findings freely available to researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders.

The Plan-EO team integrates epidemiological data from broad-spectrum molecular diagnostics with climate and environmental data derived from Earth-observation satellites, nationally representative household surveys, and other sources. The team brings together expertise in epidemiology, hydrology, bioinformatics, software and systems engineering, knowledge management, and communications.

Plan-EO is a member of the SPRINGS Project, an international research consortium supported by the European Union’s Horizon Europe program. The initiative has also received supplementary funding to estimate and project diarrheal disease burden and etiologies.

Position Summary

The University of Virginia School of Medicine seeks a Research Data Analyst to help advance Plan-EO’s research on climate-sensitive infectious diseases in tropical and subtropical regions.

This position will play an important scientific and operational leadership role within Plan-EO. The Research Data Analyst will contribute to statistical analysis, data integration, scientific writing, knowledge management, grant development, and the coordination of interdisciplinary research collaborations. The position will also help oversee daily project activities, allowing senior leadership to focus on strategic direction and scientific oversight.

The successful candidate will be a highly motivated and collaborative professional who combines analytical rigor and careful attention to detail with strong communication, organizational, and relationship-building skills. The individual must be comfortable working across disciplines, collaborating equitably with international partners, mentoring junior researchers, and representing Plan-EO at conferences and stakeholder meetings.

Responsibilities

Research and Analysis

Collaborate with the research team throughout the scientific research cycle, including exploratory analysis, scoping and evidence reviews, statistical modeling, manuscript preparation, peer review, and dissemination.
Analyze and interpret complex epidemiological, environmental, and health-related datasets.
Contribute to scientific manuscripts, reports, presentations, and other research products.
Translate technical findings into clear and engaging information for scientific, policy, and public audiences.

Data Integration and Infrastructure

Develop, document, and oversee standardized data-processing systems and reproducible research workflows.
Coordinate back-end data management within the project’s secure, shared computing environment.
Partner with UVA software developers to support the development and deployment of Plan-EO’s interactive online dashboard.
Promote consistent data-management, quality-control, documentation, and version-control practices across the project.

Knowledge Management

Help maintain Plan-EO as a current and accessible living evidence system.
Organize and manage the project’s scientific resources, datasets, documentation, analytical products, and institutional knowledge.
Establish processes that support effective collaboration and information sharing across an interdisciplinary and geographically distributed team.

Scientific and Information Governance

Collaborate respectfully and equitably with international research partners.
Support the responsible conduct of research and the appropriate stewardship of data contributed by studies and participants in low- and middle-income countries.
Help ensure compliance with applicable research protocols, data-use agreements, privacy requirements, and ethical standards.

Project Representation

Represent Plan-EO professionally at international conferences, workshops, stakeholder meetings, and online forums.
Build and maintain relationships with researchers, funders, collaborators, and other stakeholders.
Help strengthen the project’s visibility, professional network, brand identity, and scientific impact.

Mentorship

Serve as a secondary mentor to undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral researchers.
Create opportunities for experiential learning, scientific development, and professional growth for UVA students and trainees.
Provide guidance on research methods, data analysis, scientific communication, and project organization.

Grant Development

Contribute to the development and submission of competitive proposals to intramural, federal, non-federal, and international funding programs.
Support proposal writing, literature reviews, preliminary analyses, project planning, and the preparation of supporting materials.

Minimum Qualifications

Master of Public Health or an equivalent graduate degree in a quantitative, public health, or health-sciences discipline.
Graduate-level training in biostatistics, epidemiological methods, and the responsible conduct of human-subjects research.
At least four years of relevant professional experience, including experience in an analytical role within an international research environment.
Strong bioinformatics, quantitative analysis, or data-science skills, including proficiency with R and/or Python.
Experience using geographic information system tools such as ArcGIS or QGIS.
Demonstrated ability to review, synthesize, and communicate scientific evidence clearly and accurately to multiple audiences.
Experience using citation-management software such as Zotero or EndNote.
Exceptional organizational, written communication, interpersonal, and teamwork skills.
Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to take ownership of complex assignments.
Cultural sensitivity and an understanding of the importance of equitable scientific partnerships between researchers and institutions in the Global South and Global North.
Familiarity with project-management and communication platforms such as Slack, Notion, or comparable tools.
Fluency in English and conversational ability in a second widely spoken language.
Ability and willingness to travel occasionally for conferences, meetings, and project activities.

Preferred Qualifications

Proficiency or working knowledge of Spanish.
Familiarity with Stata.
Familiarity with AI-enabled research tools such as Elicit, Antigravity, Perplexity, or comparable platforms, including the ability to use these tools judiciously, ethically, and responsibly.

Physical Demands

This is primarily a sedentary position involving extensive use of desktop computers. The position occasionally requires travel to attend conferences, meetings, workshops, and other program activities.

Salary

The anticipated hiring range is $75,000–$90,000, commensurate with education and experience.

Position Type and Work Location

This is an exempt-level, benefited position. Additional information about UVA benefits is available on the UVA Human Resources website.

This is a two-year limited-term position. Continued employment beyond the initial term will depend on departmental need, satisfactory performance, and the availability of funding.

The position is based in Charlottesville, Virginia, and is eligible for a hybrid schedule requiring three days per week on Grounds. Additional on-site presence may be required based on project needs and in accordance with UVA’s remote-work guidelines.

The University of Virginia is a nationally recognized public institution of higher education and an academic medical center committed to excellence in teaching, research, patient care, and public service. UVA offers a collaborative professional environment, competitive benefits, and opportunities to contribute to research with meaningful local and global impact.

Position Introduction

The Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences Dean's Office is seeking two undergraduate students to join its Data Analysis team as Student Data Analysts.

This position provides students with practical experience in data analysis, research, reporting, and data visualization. Student Data Analysts will work with institutional data and support projects that inform decision-making across the College. Students will receive hands-on training and regular guidance as they develop skills in Excel, Power BI, data validation, analytical reasoning, and professional communication.

We are especially interested in students who would like to remain in the position for multiple semesters, allowing them to continue developing their skills and take on increasingly independent work.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain reports, dashboards, charts, and analytical models using Excel and Power BI.
Retrieve, organize, review, and validate institutional data.
Assist with enrollment, student, academic program, and other College-level analyses.
Respond to data and reporting requests from departments and Dean's Office leadership.
Research and investigate unexpected trends or inconsistencies in data.
Learn to query databases and work with institutional data sources.
Document data sources, calculations, assumptions, and analytical methods.
Summarize findings in clear language for non-technical audiences.
Assist with longer-term analytical projects from initial research through final presentation.
Manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
Handle confidential student and personnel information in accordance with FERPA and University policies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Student analysts will learn to answer three important questions about their work:

How did you arrive at that number?
Where did the data come from?
How do we know it's right?

What You'll Learn

Develop advanced Excel and Power BI skills.
Learn how professional analysts approach and validate data.
Work with real-world datasets and business questions.
Improve analytical writing and data visualization skills.
Present findings to College leadership and departmental administrators.
Complete projects that can be discussed in future job or graduate school interviews.
Receive regular feedback and professional development from the Executive Director.

Students who demonstrate strong performance and increased proficiency may be considered for additional responsibilities and advancement opportunities, subject to University processes and available funding.

Students from all DFCAS majors are encouraged to apply. Advanced data-analysis experience is not required. We are looking for students who are curious, careful, willing to learn, and interested in understanding not only what the numbers show, but why. Students with at least two semesters remaining at OU are especially encouraged to apply.

Selection Process

We want to see how you like to solve problems. The interview includes a short data-analysis exercise: you'll build a simple chart and write a brief interpretation of the data, and then we'll talk through it together. We're evaluating analytical thinking, attention to detail, and communication — not advanced Excel skills, and not how you perform under pressure. If you need help with Excel, just ask.

Use Of AI

AI tools may be used as part of the application process, interview exercise, and position when appropriate.

Applicants should be prepared to explain how they used AI and how they reviewed or verified its output. AI is considered a tool to support analytical work, not a replacement for independent judgment.

All use of AI while working with University information must comply with applicable University requirements regarding confidentiality, FERPA, information security, and institutional data.

Hiring contingent upon verification of current student status.

Must be a student in the Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences.

Skills

Basic familiarity with Microsoft Excel.
Strong written communication skills.
Attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to think critically and solve problems.
Ability to learn new software and analytical methods.
Ability to maintain confidentiality.
Ability to maintain a consistent weekly work schedule.

Zello is a voice-first communication platform, powered by our industry-leading push-to-talk technology, to improve collaboration and productivity for desk-less workers. Run 10+ well-powered product experiments end to end, from hypothesis and telemetry spec through analysis to a clear ship-or-kill call, with real impact on activation or conversion.

Work with PMs, designers, and engineers to define product metrics, events, and what success looks like.

Build and run AI-agent workflows that take the grunt work off your plate, and check what they hand back.

Turn the analysis into a clear story and a recommendation people can act on.

You've owned A/B tests end to end and can point to decisions that changed because of your work, not just dashboards you built.
You write advanced SQL on your own against a cloud warehouse, and you reach for Python when it helps.
You've already reworked how you work around AI - handing routine analysis to agents and checking their output - and you want to push that further.
You pick the right method for the data in front of you instead of running the same test every time.
You don't wait for perfect data. You build the analysis, pressure-test it, and bring a recommendation.
You make work easier for the people around you. PMs and designers find you straightforward to work with.

This role is not

A dashboard or BI-reporting job - dashboards support the work, they're not the work.
A data engineering or pipeline role - the team's got that covered.
A management role - this is a senior IC.
For someone who needs every query and metric handed to them.

Department and Project Overview

The Planetary Child Health & Enterics Observatory (Plan-EO) is an interdisciplinary research initiative and living evidence system based at the University of Virginia School of Medicine and founded and coordinated by Dr. Josh Colston.

Plan-EO works to systematically model, quantify, predict, and project the epidemiology and burden of enteric infectious diseases and their risk factors across low-resource regions of the world. The initiative makes its findings freely available to researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders.

The Plan-EO team integrates epidemiological data from broad-spectrum molecular diagnostics with climate and environmental data derived from Earth-observation satellites, nationally representative household surveys, and other sources. The team brings together expertise in epidemiology, hydrology, bioinformatics, software and systems engineering, knowledge management, and communications.

Plan-EO is a member of the SPRINGS Project, an international research consortium supported by the European Union’s Horizon Europe program. The initiative has also received supplementary funding to estimate and project diarrheal disease burden and etiologies.

Position Summary

The University of Virginia School of Medicine seeks a Research Data Analyst to help advance Plan-EO’s research on climate-sensitive infectious diseases in tropical and subtropical regions.

This position will play an important scientific and operational leadership role within Plan-EO. The Research Data Analyst will contribute to statistical analysis, data integration, scientific writing, knowledge management, grant development, and the coordination of interdisciplinary research collaborations. The position will also help oversee daily project activities, allowing senior leadership to focus on strategic direction and scientific oversight.

The successful candidate will be a highly motivated and collaborative professional who combines analytical rigor and careful attention to detail with strong communication, organizational, and relationship-building skills. The individual must be comfortable working across disciplines, collaborating equitably with international partners, mentoring junior researchers, and representing Plan-EO at conferences and stakeholder meetings.

Responsibilities

Research and Analysis

Collaborate with the research team throughout the scientific research cycle, including exploratory analysis, scoping and evidence reviews, statistical modeling, manuscript preparation, peer review, and dissemination.
Analyze and interpret complex epidemiological, environmental, and health-related datasets.
Contribute to scientific manuscripts, reports, presentations, and other research products.
Translate technical findings into clear and engaging information for scientific, policy, and public audiences.

Data Integration and Infrastructure

Develop, document, and oversee standardized data-processing systems and reproducible research workflows.
Coordinate back-end data management within the project’s secure, shared computing environment.
Partner with UVA software developers to support the development and deployment of Plan-EO’s interactive online dashboard.
Promote consistent data-management, quality-control, documentation, and version-control practices across the project.

Knowledge Management

Help maintain Plan-EO as a current and accessible living evidence system.
Organize and manage the project’s scientific resources, datasets, documentation, analytical products, and institutional knowledge.
Establish processes that support effective collaboration and information sharing across an interdisciplinary and geographically distributed team.

Scientific and Information Governance

Collaborate respectfully and equitably with international research partners.
Support the responsible conduct of research and the appropriate stewardship of data contributed by studies and participants in low- and middle-income countries.

Build and maintain relationships with researchers, funders, collaborators, and other stakeholders.
Help strengthen the project’s visibility, professional network, brand identity, and scientific impact.

Minimum Qualifications

Graduate-level training in biostatistics, epidemiological methods, and the responsible conduct of human-subjects research.
At least four years of relevant professional experience, including experience in an analytical role within an international research environment.

Experience using geographic information system tools such as ArcGIS or QGIS.
Demonstrated ability to review, synthesize, and communicate scientific evidence clearly and accurately to multiple audiences.
Experience using citation-management software such as Zotero or EndNote.
Exceptional organizational, written communication, interpersonal, and teamwork skills.
Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to take ownership of complex assignments.

Position Introduction

The Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences Dean's Office is seeking two undergraduate students to join its Data Analysis team as Student Data Analysts.

This position provides students with practical experience in data analysis, research, reporting, and data visualization. Student Data Analysts will work with institutional data and support projects that inform decision-making across the College. Students will receive hands-on training and regular guidance as they develop skills in Excel, Power BI, data validation, analytical reasoning, and professional communication.

We are especially interested in students who would like to remain in the position for multiple semesters, allowing them to continue developing their skills and take on increasingly independent work.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain reports, dashboards, charts, and analytical models using Excel and Power BI.
Retrieve, organize, review, and validate institutional data.
Assist with enrollment, student, academic program, and other College-level analyses.
Respond to data and reporting requests from departments and Dean's Office leadership.
Research and investigate unexpected trends or inconsistencies in data.
Learn to query databases and work with institutional data sources.
Document data sources, calculations, assumptions, and analytical methods.
Summarize findings in clear language for non-technical audiences.
Assist with longer-term analytical projects from initial research through final presentation.
Manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
Handle confidential student and personnel information in accordance with FERPA and University policies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Student analysts will learn to answer three important questions about their work:

How did you arrive at that number?
Where did the data come from?
How do we know it's right?

What You'll Learn

Develop advanced Excel and Power BI skills.
Learn how professional analysts approach and validate data.
Work with real-world datasets and business questions.
Improve analytical writing and data visualization skills.
Present findings to College leadership and departmental administrators.
Complete projects that can be discussed in future job or graduate school interviews.
Receive regular feedback and professional development from the Executive Director.

Students who demonstrate strong performance and increased proficiency may be considered for additional responsibilities and advancement opportunities, subject to University processes and available funding.

Students from all DFCAS majors are encouraged to apply. Advanced data-analysis experience is not required. We are looking for students who are curious, careful, willing to learn, and interested in understanding not only what the numbers show, but why. Students with at least two semesters remaining at OU are especially encouraged to apply.

Selection Process

We want to see how you like to solve problems. The interview includes a short data-analysis exercise: you'll build a simple chart and write a brief interpretation of the data, and then we'll talk through it together. We're evaluating analytical thinking, attention to detail, and communication — not advanced Excel skills, and not how you perform under pressure. If you need help with Excel, just ask.

Use Of AI

AI tools may be used as part of the application process, interview exercise, and position when appropriate.

Applicants should be prepared to explain how they used AI and how they reviewed or verified its output. AI is considered a tool to support analytical work, not a replacement for independent judgment.

All use of AI while working with University information must comply with applicable University requirements regarding confidentiality, FERPA, information security, and institutional data.

Ability to maintain a consistent weekly work schedule.

Position Overview

Kiewit Industrial & Water Engineering (KIWE) is seeking a Mechanical Data Solutions Engineer
to join our Lenexa, Kansas office. This role is responsible for developing, improving, and supporting data-driven mechanical solutions that strengthen estimating, engineering, and project delivery workflows for complex industrial projects.

The Mechanical Data Solutions Engineer partners closely with engineering, estimating, procurement, construction, and start-up teams to translate project requirements, model data, and business needs into reliable digital tools, reporting solutions, and integrated data workflows. This position plays a critical role in connecting engineering and estimating information, improving data quality, enabling model-based quantity and cost insights, and supporting consistent decision-making across project teams.

In addition to delivering high-quality data solutions, the Mechanical Data Solutions Engineer supports the growth and continuous improvement of mechanical estimating and engineering workflows through process innovation, technical collaboration, and practical implementation of digital tools.

District Overview

Kiewit Engineering Group, Inc. is a full-service engineering consulting and design firm serving a broad range of industrial markets. With more than 1,300 engineers and design professionals across all major engineering disciplines, we support the industrial, transportation, power, water/wastewater, mining, building, and oil, gas & chemical markets.

Our operations-focused engineering approach integrates over 130 years of construction expertise to deliver safe, efficient facilities — finishing projects on schedule and ensuring that Nobody Gets Hurt.

The Industrial & Water Engineering team includes process, mechanical, electrical, controls, structural, architectural, geotechnical, and civil disciplines. We specialize in EPC and design-build delivery for industrial projects in markets including:

Datacenters
Mineral Processing
Renewable Fuels
Pulp & Paper
Industrial Energy, Water & Utilities

Location

This position is based in Lenexa, Kansas
. Opportunities for flexible work are available.

Responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain data workflows that support mechanical estimating, engineering, procurement, construction, and project delivery teams.
Develop and improve processes for extracting, transforming, validating, and organizing mechanical data from models, drawings, specifications, vendor information, estimating tools, and other project systems.
Create reliable reporting and analytics solutions that provide clear visibility into quantities, scope, cost drivers, design progress, data completeness, and project trends.
Partner with mechanical engineering, estimating, BIM/VDC, procurement, construction, and project controls teams to understand business needs and translate them into practical data solutions.
Support model-based quantity takeoff, data exchange, and digital estimating workflows by improving how mechanical information is structured, connected, and reused across platforms.
Develop automation tools, dashboards, templates, and repeatable processes that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and increase confidence in mechanical data.
Establish and maintain data quality checks, validation rules, and review processes to identify missing, inconsistent, or inaccurate mechanical information.
Work with project teams to troubleshoot data issues, reconcile discrepancies, and improve the reliability of information used for estimating and decision-making.
Coordinate with internal technology, analytics, and application teams to support integration between engineering models, estimating systems, databases, reporting tools, and enterprise platforms.
Document data workflows, standards, assumptions, and tool instructions so project teams can apply solutions consistently.
Provide training and technical support to users adopting new mechanical data tools, reports, and workflows.
Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend improvements that enhance mechanical data management, automation, analytics, and model-based project delivery.
Incorporate AI-enabled tools and methods into mechanical data workflows where appropriate, ensuring solutions are developed, validated, documented, and governed through a consistent and quality-focused methodology.
Evaluate opportunities to use AI-assisted development, automation, anomaly detection, and data quality monitoring to improve speed, consistency, and reliability while maintaining human review, traceability, and practical engineering judgment.
Drive continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to standardize, simplify, and scale mechanical data solutions across projects and teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, engineering technology, data analytics, computer science, construction management, or a related technical field; equivalent practical experience may be considered.
5+ years of experience supporting engineering, estimating, BIM/VDC, construction, or project delivery workflows, preferably within industrial, water, EPC, or design-build environments.
Strong understanding of mechanical systems, mechanical estimating concepts, model-based quantities, engineering deliverables, and project data structures.
Experience working with data from engineering models, drawings, specifications, estimating systems, databases, spreadsheets, and other project delivery platforms.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including advanced formulas, structured tables, data cleanup, and large dataset analysis.
Experience with Power BI, Power Query, data modeling, dashboards, reporting, or similar business intelligence and analytics tools preferred.
Working knowledge of SQL, relational databases, data transformation, data validation, or data integration concepts.
Experience with BIM/model data, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Revit, AutoCAD, Navisworks, Smart 3D, or similar engineering and design platforms preferred.
Ability to develop repeatable tools, templates, reports, and workflows that improve data quality, reduce manual effort, and support consistent decision-making.
Strong analytical skills with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to identify missing, inconsistent, or inaccurate information.
Ability to translate business needs into practical data solutions and communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical users.
Proven ability to collaborate across engineering, estimating, BIM/VDC, procurement, construction, project controls, technology, and analytics teams.
Strong documentation skills, including the ability to clearly define workflows, assumptions, standards, validation steps, and user instructions.
Self-motivated and continuous improvement oriented, with the ability to manage priorities, troubleshoot issues, and deliver reliable solutions in a schedule-driven environment.
Familiarity with AI-enabled tools, automation concepts, or emerging data technologies, with an understanding of how to apply them responsibly to improve engineering, estimating, analytics, and data quality workflows.
Ability to support evolving AI and automation practices through consistent documentation, validation, governance, and quality control methods that promote repeatable and trustworthy outcomes.

Run 10+ well-powered product experiments end to end, from hypothesis and telemetry spec through analysis to a clear ship-or-kill call, with real impact on activation or conversion.

A dashboard or BI-reporting job - dashboards support the work, they're not the work.
A data engineering or pipeline role - the team's got that covered.
